newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Forecast-CHH Q1 seen hit by pulp prices.
newsitem.headline: Forecast-CHH Q1 seen hit by pulp prices.

text.p: Analysts expect Carter Holt Harvey Ltd to post a net profit before abnormals of around NZ$45-50 million when the forest products company reports its first quarter result on Thursday.
This would compare with NZ$56 million in the same June quarter of last year - considered then as being at the bottom of the pulp and paper cycle.
But this time there are signs of improvement in pulp prices, which have come off from a low of around US$500 per tonne to about US$580 currently.
Major producers have signalled price increases effective for July 1, which came on top of increases scheduled for May.
Low prices over the quarter would impact on profitability but several other factors were likely to come into play, not the least being increased competition in domestic packaging.

"We are expecting this quarter's result to be lower than any of the quarters of last year, reflecting the combination of cyclically weak product prices, the strength of the New Zealand dollar and a number of one-off factors," David Stanley at brokers Doyle Paterson Brown said.
CHH is still in the process of re-organising some of its business units, which was likely to incur short term costs but which would bring long term benefits.

CHH's 30 percent associate, Compania de Petroleos de Chile SA (Copec) this week reported a slight improvement in net earnings to 60.8 billion pesos, which should translate into a contribution of about NZ$24 million for CHH.
John Cairns at Cavill White Securities said that while the result would doubtless reflect difficult trading conditions, he was reasonably upbeat.
Cairns noted that the final quarter's profit came in at NZ$80 million and he expected strength in CHH's international business to go some way to offset domestic pressures.
Analysts expect CHH to report a net profit of around $300 million for the year to March, 1998, which would be NZ$50 million improvement on the financial year just past.
CHH, just over half owned by International Paper, last traded at NZ$3.75.
